reason: Both correctly refused to name a part blind and got the airflow (filter and vent hose) cleared first, but Conversation 2 handled the endpoint correctly: once airflow was clear and it was still cold, it narrowed to heater/thermal cut-out/thermostat, explained the cut-out points to an underlying cause, and escalated to an engineer because testing is needed, exactly matching the homeowner's 'no multimeter' situation. Conversation 1 ignored the customer's statement that they cannot do continuity tests, never escalated, and its final turn merely told them to drag the unit out of the alcove to read the label, which does not move them toward a safe resolution. Conversation 2 also consistently said to switch off and unplug before each check, whereas Conversation 1 did not. Conversation 1 was more efficient (combining filter and vent in one step) and did at least try for the model number, but efficiency does not outweigh the missed escalation.
